body:
Hi, I'm trying to migrate my config from vim-sandwich to mini. I hope I could get some help.

I want to make 'c' to add code block in markdown.

- If the target to surround is single line, surround with "`". 
- If the target is multi line surround with "```". 

```
asd -> `asd`

asd\nasd -> ```asd\nasd```
```

I'm not sure how to do "GETINPUT()" 
```
["c"] = {
    output = function(a)
        local content = GETINPUT()
        if string.find(content, "\n") == nil then
            return { left = "`", right = "`" }
        else
            return { left = "```\n", right = "\n```\n" }
        end
    end,
},
```

comment_data.body:
There is no easy method to do this, because callable `output` specification gets called without arguments and no guarantees at what Neovim state it does so. But it is an interesting use case.

Here is my closest attempt:
```lua
require('mini.surround').setup({
  custom_surroundings = {
    c = {
      output = function()
        local is_visual = _G.is_visual
        _G.is_visual = nil
        local mark_from = is_visual and "'<" or "'["
        local mark_to = is_visual and "'>" or "']"
        local n_content_lines = vim.fn.line(mark_to) - vim.fn.line(mark_from)
        if n_content_lines == 0 then return { left = '`', right = '`' } end
        return { left = '```\n', right = '\n```\n' }
      end,
    },
  },
})

local rhs = [[<Cmd>lua _G.is_visual=true<CR>:<C-u>lua MiniSurround.add('visual')<CR>]]
vim.keymap.set('x', 'sa', rhs, { silent = true })
```

Quick notes:
- It doesn't compute whole content per se, but directly decides whether it is single or multiple line. It does so by utilizing information from marks depending on mode.
- As it seems to always be executed in Normal mode, there needs to be a way to distinguish when adding is performed in Visual or Operator-pending mode. This is the cause of all the `_G.is_visual` trickery. If you decide to only apply this in Visual mode, then no need for that.
- It doesn't really work when multiline text is indented. It is by design of 'mini.surround' that it will place left surrounding part at the left of the first non-blank character in linewise mode. You can try `config.respect_selection_type = true` and `{ left = '```', right = '```' }` as returned value, but it will indent the code (again, by design to account for more common use cases).


------

Another solution would be to make a prompt for user to add extra key press and tell which type of code surrounding they want. For example, with `vim.fn.getcharstr()` and information message with `print()`.

------

That said, my **proper** solution would be to advise you to use separate surroundings for single and multi line cases. The first one is plain `` ` ``, the second one can be mapped to `c`.
comment_data.bodyHTML:
There is no easy method to do this, because callable output specification gets called without arguments and no guarantees at what Neovim state it does so. But it is an interesting use case.

Here is my closest attempt:

require('mini.surround').setup({
  custom_surroundings = {
    c = {
      output = function()
        local is_visual = _G.is_visual
        _G.is_visual = nil
        local mark_from = is_visual and "'<" or "'["
        local mark_to = is_visual and "'>" or "']"
        local n_content_lines = vim.fn.line(mark_to) - vim.fn.line(mark_from)
        if n_content_lines == 0 then return { left = '`', right = '`' } end
        return { left = '```\n', right = '\n```\n' }
      end,
    },
  },
})

local rhs = [[<Cmd>lua _G.is_visual=true<CR>:<C-u>lua MiniSurround.add('visual')<CR>]]
vim.keymap.set('x', 'sa', rhs, { silent = true })

Quick notes:

  • It doesn't compute whole content per se, but directly decides whether it is single or multiple line. It does so by utilizing information from marks depending on mode.
  • As it seems to always be executed in Normal mode, there needs to be a way to distinguish when adding is performed in Visual or Operator-pending mode. This is the cause of all the _G.is_visual trickery. If you decide to only apply this in Visual mode, then no need for that.
  • It doesn't really work when multiline text is indented. It is by design of 'mini.surround' that it will place left surrounding part at the left of the first non-blank character in linewise mode. You can try config.respect_selection_type = true and { left = '```', right = '```' } as returned value, but it will indent the code (again, by design to account for more common use cases).

Another solution would be to make a prompt for user to add extra key press and tell which type of code surrounding they want. For example, with vim.fn.getcharstr() and information message with print().

That said, my proper solution would be to advise you to use separate surroundings for single and multi line cases. The first one is plain `, the second one can be mapped to c.

comment_data.body:
Thanks! 

I ended up with this to make it work with indent.
This is so messy, but just for the record if anyone needs it.

```
        ["c"] = {
            -- https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/discussions/462
            output = function()
                -- is_visual doesn't work
                -- local is_visual = vim.tbl_contains({ 'v', 'V', '\22' }, vim.fn.mode())
                -- local mark_from = is_visual and "'<" or "'["
                -- local mark_to = is_visual and "'>" or "']"
                local mark_from = "'<"
                local mark_to = "'>"
                local startline = vim.fn.line(mark_from)
                local endline = vim.fn.line(mark_to)
                local n_content_lines = endline - startline
                if n_content_lines == 0 then
                    return { left = "`", right = "`" }
                end
                local firstline = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0, startline - 1, startline, false)
                local _, indent = string.find(firstline[1], '^%s*')
                if indent ~= nil then
                    return { left = "```\n" .. string.rep(" ", indent) , right = "\n" .. string.rep(" ", indent) .. "```\n" }
                else
                    return { left = "```\n", right = "\n```\n" }
                end
            end,
        },
```
